chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi Basir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Things are referred to us which we do not know in the Book of Allah nor the Sunna, should we exercise reason in them? He said: No, for indeed if you were to get it right you would not be rewarded, and if you were to err you would have lied upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exercising reason in matters not found in the Quran and Sunna according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the practice of *nazar* (independent reasoning) for deriving new rulings outside explicit textual evidence. He establishes that while correct reasoning might be coincidentally right, it lacks the divine guarantee of reward, whereas error is deemed a direct falsehood against Allah, underscoring the Shia emphasis on strict adherence to the Quran and Sunna over speculative deduction.
